emit its cached progress event; further progress events arrive on the same target."

Check originating subscription and visit eligibility before decoding each packet. Retirement immediately prevents subsequent admission, including additional packets emitted before startup returns; do not depend solely on physical listener removal. README.md: "A retired visit
accepts no new progress events."

Separate admission, retained audit and visible publication. Record each admitted event exactly once when decoding completes, including after retirement or disposal; check originating visit validity before visible publication. README.md: "Every accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding
finishes, including work accepted before the visit closes." It also states: "Removing a listener does not retract a decode
that already started. Closing or replacing the visit stops visible progress;
new visits remain live." Reopening the identical file creates a distinct visit.

Coordinate cleanup and ownership across callback-capable startup and cancellation. Retire old ownership before cleanup can reenter navigation; when an older operation resumes, prevent it from overwriting newer ownership and clean up its retired resources. Preserve idempotent cancellation and disposal. README.md: "Selection and hiding may themselves cancel an old handle and synchronously
receive newer navigation; the newer navigation keeps ownership." Also: "Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels transfers; work already accepted
for audit remains retained." A provisional cleanup handle is an implementation option, not a mandated public interface.

Keep accepted retries bound to their entry file and visit. Cancel the prior transfer before enqueueing, preserve exactly one accepted command and record across cancellation navigation, cancel the resulting transfer if its visit ended, and suppress retired queued notices. README.md: "The accepted old retry must still enqueue and record once after such navigation.
Its newly created transfer is canceled immediately if its visit has ended; this
does not remove its retained queue record." Also: "Queued notices are visible output: a notice
from a retired visit must not be sent, including after reopening the same file." Preserve independent workspace counters and cancellation.

Keep the repair within reception and necessary lifecycle coordination. Preserve queue and notice shapes and adapter interfaces. README.md: "Every queue record remains exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`;" and "Notices remain\n`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: \"queued\"}`." Do not transfer unrelated diagnostic-consumer policies into this repair.

Ownership outliving a view, a synchronous API name, a passing check or generic preservation wording alone does not establish this deadline. If evidence permits continued scheduling or discard, follow it instead.

Clean captured old resources while preserving new ones. Keep repeated cancellation and removal inert, and preserve the host's removal-before-callback contract.

Hide, switch and dispose inside startup and unlisten callbacks. Check the current visit, later updates, listener ownership, physical cancellation and final cleanup.

rules.body: The repair targets panel progress, while queue records, queued notices and public transfer behavior must remain unchanged.

Compare record shape, cardinality, queued notices and returned handles across selection, retry, cancellation and navigation reentry.

Reopen the same object and channel, complete old decoding late and interleave two independent workspaces. Check isolation of old effects and continued operation of the new visit.

rules.body: A fresh online-mode query remains offline from mount through unmount, has not entered execution and has lost its final observer.

This target obligation is independent of refetchOnReconnect. Preserve other legitimate execution, settlement and state restoration.

Reconnect after departure, depart after continuation is queued and vary refetchOnReconnect. Check zero entry or entry with an already-canceled signal as the contract permits, rather than only final flags.

rules.body: Accessing cancellation capability records actual consumption synchronously. The query shares that record, while each attempt owns its controller and completion identity.

Do not invent consumption from observer departure, paused status or an attempt object's existence. This policy does not apply when the target lacks the lazy shared mechanism.
Check consumption records and controller ownership before access, on later and repeated access, across attempt replacement and during observer reuse.

rules.body: Multiple observers share work. Canceling consumed work physically terminates it and restores previous query state.

Observer departure changes that observer's lifetime; remaining observers continue sharing. Cancellation settles the originating attempt and restores prior data and status under the contract. Unknown departures remain inert.
Preserve physical abort, prior-state restoration, originating-attempt settlement, later subscription reuse and repeated invalid unsubscription behavior.
One departure must not terminate shared work still needed by others. An unknown unsubscription must not be treated as final-observer departure.

Remove one observer while another remains, repeat departures and unsubscribe unknown observers, then cancel consumed work and resubscribe. Check shared invocation counts, physical termination and restored data/status.

Do not coalesce events that must each be processed. Use the current task's interval; the historical 120 ms value is not a default or new deadline.

rules.body: A reusable deferred task invokes a synchronous save or consumer callback that can enqueue another value or flush reentrantly.

Capture the old value; retire that batch's pending state and timer before invoking its consumer. Work enqueued by that callback belongs to the next batch. Timer cancellation alone does not establish consumption.
Consume the old value once. Outer cleanup must not erase callback-created work or consume it as the old batch. Preserve later reuse, valid empty values and the existing absence sentinel.
Saving is not a terminal state. Do not replace explicit None/null/nil sentinel checks with truthiness tests, or discard valid empty content.
Inside the consumer, enqueue another value and invoke nested flush. Check old-batch cardinality, survival of the new batch, its next deadline and successful later reuse.

rules.body: Packets decode to complete replacement frames, completions may reverse reception order, and the current task or protocol explicitly defines display freshness by packet arrival within a logical display owner.

Determine visit-local, attempt-local and cross-retry scope from the current protocol; resetting a scope must not admit stale attempt results.

Preserve each independently required audit effect even for a frame suppressed from display. Later legitimate values may decrease or reset. Respect owner eligibility as well as order, including during reentrant publication.

Loaded bytes, completion time and numeric monotonicity are not arrival identity. Do not drop required delta events. If the source defines server revisions or a different ordering policy, use that policy rather than importing arrival order.

Reverse decode completion; let the later-received frame have a lower value; emit or finish another frame synchronously while painting. Verify no rollback, retained audits, and correct ordering scope across retry, navigation and same-source reopening.

rules.body: The current source retains a history or audit effect for admitted work after navigation, while UI publication belongs to its originating visit. Decoding may complete immediately or after suspension.

Capture admission identity, including visit and attempt where present. Complete the retained audit according to its cardinality contract; then recheck the originating visit immediately before visible publication. Recheck after callback-capable auditing because it may navigate.

Listener removal, a newer display and old-view retirement do not retract an already admitted retained effect. Preserve its original identity and required count, suppress retired-visit painting and keep the current visit's valid delivery live.

Do not use one early eligibility check for both audit and display. Retained audit never authorizes stale UI publication. If the current source explicitly revokes or discards history, follow that policy rather than imposing retention.

Complete admitted work after hide, switch, cancellation/retry where supported, disposal and same-source reopening. Check audit count and identity separately from display; navigate inside the audit callback and verify publication permission is checked again.

rules.body: The current implementation documents a persistent document buffer, store or coordinator that outlives a view owning only its current live/status subscription.

Preserve original identity/text/payload semantics, independent document buffers, same-document reopening, continuing persistence responsibility, document presentation and current-view status filtering. Determine the actual owner from the current source.

View detachment does not imply cancellation. Persistent ownership alone does not establish a before-return departure flush; derive settlement scheduling from the current contract. Do not transfer durable retention to a transient preview with a discard-on-hide policy.

Switch, close, dispose and reopen with pending work. Check eventual persistence to the original owner, buffer reuse, subscription release, independent documents and current-view output separately; check immediate settlement only when the source requires that deadline.

rules.body: A deferred result can arrive after terminal close/dispose of its originating modal. Operation invocation/completion and an application-shell or other consumer have independent lifetimes.

Check that originating modal's current closed state in the completion continuation, before assigning its value or emitting a write. An admission-time snapshot is insufficient, including closure during notify. Preserve result acquisition, assignment, write and any existing publication in their original synchronous order. Where an existing publication follows a callback-capable write, a post-write closure check protects that publication; apply it only to that source's existing effect.

Keep notify invocation and original-payload completion/returned delivery outside the modal-effect guard, including calls made after close. Closing suppresses modal mutation/write/publication, not the independent operation result. Preserve value and payload identity, snapshot shape, controller verbs, terminal closure, separate modal instances, actual unmount cleanup and the existing disposeChild behavior.

Limit the repair to the modal subscription; preserve shell independence without inventing its implementation. Do not add publication where absent, defer callbacks, impose freshness/request supersession, add cancellation or import persistent-buffer policies. Post-write reentry is a conditional defensive checkpoint, not a universal host guarantee. Rejection handling, callback exceptions, additional disposeChild semantics and concurrent-result ordering remain unspecified unless current source supplies them.

Check completion while open, after close, after dispose, during notify closure, run after close, multiple completions and actual unmount cleanup. Observe modal value, write, any existing publication and returned payload separately. Check unchanged disposeChild, independent instances and shell policy. Where writes can reenter closure and publication exists, verify no subsequent publication but continued original-result delivery. Syntax/acceptance alone does not prove behavioral completeness or causality.
